[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Web Application Protection — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to inspect inbound HTTP/S traffic destined for web application endpoints and block requests that match known attack patterns before they reach the application.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to inspect and filter HTTP/S traffic for application-layer attack patterns
- Protection against common web application attack classes (injection, cross-site scripting, malformed protocol abuse, etc.)
- Bot mitigation and rate limiting at the application entry point
- Logging and alerting on blocked and suspicious traffic

**Out of Scope**:
- In-process application runtime protection (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RASP-2.7.20)
- Network-layer traffic filtering (see Network Security domain)
- API authorization enforcement (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11, GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIAZ-2.7.12)
- Security controls, ruleset selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- A WAF capability SHALL be positioned in the request path for all externally accessible web application endpoints.
- WAF rule decisions SHALL be logged regardless of allow/deny outcome to enable retrospective analysis.
- WAF SHOULD operate initially in detection mode in new deployments to establish a baseline before enforcement mode is enabled, in order to avoid false-positive blocking.
- WAF rule sets SHALL be kept current; the architecture must account for ongoing rule maintenance as new attack patterns emerge.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#traffic-inspection]

#### Traffic Inspection

**Architectural intent**: Evaluate inbound HTTP/S requests against patterns associated with known attack classes before they reach application logic.

**Design guidance**:
- Inspection SHALL cover at minimum the OWASP Top 10 application attack categories at a request pattern level.
- The WAF SHALL operate inline in the request path, not as an out-of-band passive sensor.
- Encrypted traffic inspection SHALL be architecturally supported; TLS termination placement must be addressed in the Reference Architecture.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#request-disposition]

#### Request Disposition

**Architectural intent**: Provide consistent, auditable enforcement of request policy.

**Design guidance**:
- Request blocks SHALL be logged with the matching rule, request metadata, and source identity where available.
- Legitimate traffic blocked by false-positive rules SHALL have a defined exception path that does not require disabling rule enforcement broadly.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#alerting-and-observability]

#### Alerting and Observability

**Architectural intent**: Provide visibility into attack patterns targeting the application landscape.

**Design guidance**:
- WAF events SHALL be forwarded to the enterprise security monitoring capability (SecOps domain).
- High-confidence attack detections SHOULD generate real-time alerts for security operations triage.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inbound Request | Inbound | End User / API Consumer | HTTP/S request received for inspection |
| Forwarded Request | Outbound | Web Application Backend | Inspected and approved request forwarded to application |
| Event Stream | Outbound | SecOps SIEM/Monitoring | WAF decisions and attack events forwarded for detection |
| Block Response | Outbound | End User / API Consumer | Error response returned to blocked requestors |
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

The WAF advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by applying explicit request-level inspection at the application boundary — no request is implicitly trusted to be benign based on network origin or authenticated identity alone.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the SC (System and Communications Protection) family — boundary protection and traffic filtering at the application layer — and the SI (System and Information Integrity) family, which addresses protection against malicious code and input-based attack vectors.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-WAF-2.7.19.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- TLS termination placement significantly affects what the WAF can inspect; architecture must define where TLS is terminated relative to WAF positioning.
- WAF availability is in the critical path for all web traffic; high availability and failover behavior must be addressed in the Reference Architecture.
- WAF is a preventive/detective capability and is complementary to, not a replacement for, application-layer input validation in application code.
